to advance, to proceed, to progress; to go forth, to move forward, to move onward
to proceed; to carry on, to go on, to keep going, to move along, to move on
to result, to follow (to happen as a consequence)
to prepare, to set about (doing something)
to aim, to intend, to mean

la:verb:eo.html:
ĕo, īvi or ii (īt, ; cf.
Lachm. ad Lucr. vol. 2, p. 206 sq.: isse, issem, etc., for ivisse, etc.,; ; ; et saep.: isti, Turp. ap. : istis,, etc., v. Neue Formenl. 2, 515), īre (inf. pass. irier, ), ĭtum, v. n.
root i-, Sanscr. ēmi, go; Gr. εἶμι; causat. ἵημι = jacio,
, to go (of every kind of motion of animate or inanimate things), to walk, ride, sail, fly, move, pass, etc. (very freq. in all periods and sorts of writing).
Lit.
In gen.: eo ad forum,: i domum, sq.: nos priores ibimus,: i in crucem,go and be hanged!; cf.: i in malam crucem,; ; : i in malam rem hinc,: iens in Pompeianum,: subsidio suis ierunt,: quom it dormitum,; id Most. 3, 2, 4; 16; et saep, cf.: dormitum, lusum,: cubitum,; ; ; ; et saep.—Poet. with the acc. of the terminus: ibis Cecropios portus, Loers.: Sardoos recessus,; cf.: hinc Afros,.—With a cognate acc.: ire vias,: exsequias,: pompam funeris, et saep.: non explorantur eundae vitandaeque viae,: animae ad lumen iturae,: ego ire in Piraeum volo,; cf.: visere ad aliquam,; : videre,: ire pedibus,on foot,: equis,: curru,; ; cf.: in equis,: in raeda,: super equos,; and with equis to be supplied,: puppibus,; cf.: cum classe Pisas, et saep.: concedere quo poterunt undae, cum pisces ire nequibunt?.—
Of things: alvus non it,; so, sanguis naribus,: Euphrates jam mollior undis,: sudor per artus,: fucus in artus,: telum (with volare),: trabes,i. e. to give way, sink, et saep.: in semen ire (asparagum),to go to seed,; so ; cf.: in corpus (juvenes),: sanguis it in sucos,turns into,.—
In partic.
To go or proceed against with hostile intent, to march against: quos fugere credebant, infestis signis ad se ire viderunt,: ad hostem,: contra hostem,; cf. : adversus hostem,: in hostem,; et saep.; cf.: in Capitolium,to go against, to attack,.—
Pregn., to pass away, disappear (very rare): saepe hominem paulatim cernimus ire,; cf. ; .
Trop.
In gen., to go, pass, proceed, move, advance: ire in opus alienum,: in dubiam imperii servitiique aleam,: in alteram causam praeceps ierat,: in rixam,: in lacrimas,; : in poenas, et saep.: ire per singula,; cf. ; ; : ad quem (modum) non per gradus itur, et saep.: dicite qua sit eundum,: ire infitias, v. infitiae: Latina debent cito pariter ire,: aliae contradictiones eunt interim longius,: in eosdem semper pedes ire (compositio),

: cum per omnes et personas et affectus eat (comoedia),; cf. ; : Phrygiae per oppida facti Rumor it,: it clamor caelo,: factoque in secula ituro, Laetantur tribuisse locum,to go down to posterity,; cf. with a subject-sentence: ibit in saecula, fuisse principem, cui, etc.,.—

In partic.
Pub. law t. t.
Pedibus ire, or simply ire in aliquam sententiam, in voting, to go over or accede to any opinion (opp. discedere, v. h. v. II. B. 2. b.): cum omnes in sententiam ejus pedibus irent,: pars major eorum qui aderant in eandem sententiam ibat,; ; fin.—Pass. impers.: in quam sententiam cum pedibus iretur,: ibatur in eam sententiam,: itum in sententiam,; .—And opp. to the above,
Ire in alia omnia, to vote against a bill, v. alius, II.—
Mercant. t. t. for vēneo, to go for, be sold at a certain price, : tot Pontus eat, tot Lydia nummis,.—
Pregn., of time, to pass by, pass away: it dies,; ; : anni,; cf.: anni more fluentis aquae,.—
With the accessory notion of result, to go, proceed, turn out, happen: incipit res melius ire quam putaram,; cf. : prorsus ibat res,; : postquam omnia fatis Caesaris ire videt,.—Hence the wish: sic eat, so may he fare: sic eat quaecunque Romana lugebit hostem,; Cort.; 2, 304; . —
Constr. with a supine, like the Gr. μέλλειν, to go or set about, to prepare, to wish, to be about to do any thing: si opulentus it petitum pauperioris gratiam, etc.,; : quod uti prohibitum irem, quod in me esset, meo labori non parsi, Cato ap. Fest. s. v. PARSI, p. 242 Müll.; so, perditum gentem universam,: ultum injurias, scelera,; : servitum Grais matribus, et saep.: bonorum praemia ereptum eunt,.—Hence the construction of the inf. pass. iri with the supine, in place of an inf. fut. pass.: mihi omne argentum redditum iri,: mihi istaec videtur praeda praedatum irier, et saep.—Poet. also with inf.: seu pontum carpere remis Ibis,: attollere facta regum,: fateri,—
Imp. i, eas, eat, etc., since the Aug. period more freq. a mocking or indignant expression, go then, go now: i nunc et cupidi nomen amantis habe,; so, i nunc,; 9, 105; 17, 57; ; (3, 27, 22 M.); ; : i, sequere Italiam ventis,; so, i,: fremunt omnibus locis: Irent, crearent consules ex plebe,

senses: alternative form of ego (attested in the 6th c. AD; see also the pagan inscription quoted below)

la:adv:eo.html:
ĕō, adv.
old dat. and abl. form of pron. stem i; cf. is
.
In locat. and abl. uses,
Of place=in eo loco, there, in that place (rare): quid (facturus est) cum tu eo quinque legiones haberes?: quo loco ... ibi ... eoque,: eo loci,; ; so trop.: eo loci, in that condition: res erat eo jam loci, ut, etc.,; ; .—
Of cause=eā re.
Referring to a cause or reason before given, therefore, on that account, for that reason: is nunc dicitur venturus peregre: eo nunc commenta est dolum,; : dederam litteras ad te: eo nunc ero brevior,; ; ; ; ; et saep.—So with conjunctions, eoque, et eo, eo quoque, in adding any thing as a consequence of what precedes, and for that reason: absolute pares, et eo quoque innumerabiles,: impeditius eoque hostibus incautum,: per gentes integras et eo feroces,; —
Referring to a foll. clause, giving
a cause or reason, with quia, quoniam, quod, etc.; so with quia: eo fit, quia mihi plurimum credo,; id. Capt. 1, 1, 2: nunc eo videtur foedus, quia, etc.,; : quia scripseras, eo te censebam, etc.,; ; .—With quoniam: haec eo notavi, quoniam, etc.,.—With quod: quod ... non potueritis, eo vobis potestas erepta sit,; ; ; ; so, neque eo ... quod,; .—
A purpose, motive or reason, with quo, ut, ne; and after negatives, with quo, quin, and subj.—So with quo: eo scripsi, quo plus auctoritatis haberem,; ; so, non eo ... quo,: neque eo ... quo,; .—With ut: haec eo scripsi, ut intellegeres,; ; .—With ne: ; : quod ego non eo vereor, ne mihi noceat,; .—With quin: non eo haec dico, quin quae tu vis ego velim,; . —
Of measure or degree—with words of comparison, so much, by so much—followed by quo (= tanto ... quanto): quae eo fructuosiores fiunt, quo calidior terra aratur,: eo gravior est dolor, quo culpa major,; ; so with quantum: quantum juniores patrum plebi se magis insinuabant, eo acrius contra tribuni tendebant, etc.,; : quanto longius abscederent, eo, etc.,. —Esp. freq. the formulae, eo magis, eo minus, so much the worse (the less), followed by quo, quod, quoniam, si, ut, ne: eo magis, quo tanta penuria est in omni honoris gradu,: eo minus veritus navibus, quod in littore molli, etc.,; ; : eo magis, quoniam, etc., Cels. praef. p. 14, 12 Müll.: nihil admirabilius fieri potest, eoque magis, si ea sunt in adulescente,; : eo diligentius ut ne parvula quidem titubatione impediremur,; : ego illa extuli et eo quidem magis, ne quid ille superiorum meminisse me putaret,.— In this combination eo often expresses also the idea of cause (cf. B. 1. supra): hoc probis pretiumst. Eo mihi magis lubet cum probis potius quam cum improbis vivere,: solliciti tamen et anxii sunt; eoque magis, quod se ipsi continent et coercent,; and some passages may be classed under either head: dederam triduo ante litteras ad te. Eo nunc ero brevior,; ; ; ; .
In dat. uses.
With the idea of motion, to that place, thither (=in eum locum): eo se recipere coeperunt,: uti eo cum introeas, circumspicias, uti inde exire possit,: eo tela conicere, Auct. B. Afr. 72: eo respicere,; so, followed by quo, ubi, unde: non potuit melius pervenirier eo, quo nos volumus,: venio nunc eo, quo me fides ducit,: ibit eo quo vis, etc.,: (venit) eo, ubi non modo res erat, etc.,; ; : eo, unde discedere non oportuit, revertamur,; ; ; so (late Lat.) with loci: perducendum eo loci, ubi actum sit,; .—
Transf.
With the idea of addition, thereto, in addition to that, besides: accessit eo, ut milites ejus, etc.,: accedit eo, quod, etc.,.—
With the idea of tendency, to that end, with that purpose, to this result: hoc autem eo spectabat, ut eam a Philippo corruptam diceret,: haec eo pertinet oratio, ut ipsa virtus se sustentare posse videretur,: hoc eo valebat, ut, etc.,.—
With the idea of degree or extent, to that degree or extent, so far, to such a point: eo scientiae progredi,: postquam res publica eo magnificentiae venerit, gliscere singulos,; ; : eo magnitudinis procedere,; ; : ubi jam eo consuetudinis adducta res est, ut, etc.,; , 27, 12; 32, 18, 8 al.; : eo insolentiae processit,: eo rerum ventum erat, ut, etc.,; .— With gen., ; ; ; ; ; § 9: eo rem jam adducam, ut nihil divinationis opus sit,: res eo est deducta, ut, etc.,; ; .—
Of time, up to the time, until, so long, usually with usque, and followed by dum, donec: usque eo premere capita, dum illae captum amitterent,; ; : eo usque flagitatus est, donec ad exitium dederetur,; : eo usque vivere, donec, etc.,; cf. ; .—Rarely by quamdiu: eo usque, quamdiu ad fines barbaricos veniretur,.

la:adv:eodem.html:
ĕōdem, adv.
old dat. and abl. of idem
, of place.
Of the place in which, with gen. loci, in the same place (rare): res eodem est loci quo reliquisti,: additi eodem (i. e. in Aventino) novi cives,: arduum est eodem loci potentiam et concordiam esse,; ; .—
Of the place to which.
To the same place, to the same point: Orgetorix omnes clientes obaeratosque suos eodem conduxit,; ; : ego pol te redigam eodem unde ortus es,: eodem accedit servitus, sudor, sitis,; prol. alt. 26; ; ; .—
Transf.
To the same thing, to the same point or purpose: quid si accedit eodem, ut tenuis antea fueris,: accedit eodem volgi voluntas,: eodem pertinet quod,; .—
To the same person or persons: eodemque honores poenasque congeri, i. e. in eundem civem,: eodemque adjungas quos natura putes asperos,.
